text: Verify knowledge picked up somewhere and make it your own. Do not trust retellings, quotations torn from context, and “expert” opinions on social networks. If you come across interesting information, make an effort to find the primary source—the author's text, the original research, eyewitness accounts... Such behavior is a sign of intellectual maturity. And this especially concerns spiritual practices. It is important to pass any knowledge or technique through the filter of your own experience and sensations, to draw conclusions, and to adapt it to yourself. Otherwise the most important principle of the first stage of yoga is violated—Asteya—translated from Sanskrit as non-appropriation of what belongs to others (or more simply, non-stealing). In relation to asanas, the consequences manifest as a lack of effect or even injuries, and in the case of pranayamas your energetic framework may even be destroyed—that is, a flow of meaningless destructive events and psychological states may be set off...
